newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr Lyonnais head says swindle sums "fabrication".
newsitem.headline: Cr Lyonnais head says swindle sums "fabrication".

text.p: Credit Lyonnais chairman Jean Jean Peyrelevade said on Tuesday that allegations officials of the French bank had swindled the state-controlled institution of five billion francs were a "fabrication."
He told the national assemly finance commission he did not see how it was possible to state before the end of legal proceedings now under way "that people are guilty and for such amounts...
"If there have been swindles, these amounts are a fabrication. They are overestimated, certainly enormously overestimated," he said. The "true amounts of money swindled will never reach that amount."
Credit Lyonnais nearly collapsed as a result of a fateful lending spree at the end of the 1980s and beginnning of the 1990s but now is on the road to recovery thanks to huge amounts of state aid.

Last week, Charles de Courson, a member of the state holding company selling off the bank's troubled assets, told the finance commission he expected "100 cases to be levelled against directors or officials of the bank whose now uncovered swindles total five billion francs."

Peyrelvade, appointed by the government to clean up Credit Lyonnais's finances, added such publicity made the bank's task of recovery even harder and underlined the allegations had been made against former officials.
The bank, which lost 21 billion francs between 1992 and 1994 and limped back into the black in 1995 with a 13 million franc profit, is to due to report its 1996 results.
Analysts expect it to post a 150 million franc profit for 1996 but say earnings should be much bigger in 1997.

Asked about estimates the final cost to the French government of the rescue of Credit Lyonnais is likely to be 130 billion francs, Peyrelevade said, "The idea that it will be around one billion francs is unhappily realistic."
He added it was important to underline that the lending follies which led to the bank's near downfall were over.
"It is very important to distinguish very carefully the past from the present," he said. "The new Credit Lyonnais is a bank which functions normally, whose recovery is under way," he said.
He added that privatisation in the second half of 1998 "of a Credit Lyonnais which has become well dimensioned, perfectly profitable and perfectly viable is in my opinion completely possible."

The French government is to present a plan to the European Union for approval to ready the bank for privatisation later this month. It will be the fourth big state help package in three years for the bank.
